newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - March 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - March 5.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Wednesday's Daily Variety:

* LAS VEGAS - Jack Valenti said at ShoWest '97 Tuesday that box office and admissions were up slightly last year, but production and marketing cost increases outpaced those gains. The Motion Picture Associationn of America president also told delegates that the organization pegged 1996 box office at $5.91 billion, with ticket sales hitting 1.34 billion. Those represent respective increases of 7.6 percent and 6 percent from the prior year.

* HOLLYWOOD - Media Equities International, a newly formed partnership made up of a group of former entertainment executives, has made an equity investment of $3 million in newly issued shares of Dove Entertainment Inc common stock. Dove Entertainment is the Los Angeles-based book publisher and TV and film production-distribution company run by Michael Viner and his wife, Deborah Raffin. With their investment, MEI gets about 20 percent of Dove stock, or 1.2 million shares, with about 6.5 million shares outstanding. MEI also will receive a warrant giving it the option to increase its stake in Dove at increasing levels above the current market price.

* NEW YORK - In what has become a hallmark of his films, John Sayles' new "Men With Guns" was financed with innovative funding sources: a newly formed production company of the Independent Film Channel and Paul Allen, in his first foray into indie film. The cable channel Wednesday will announce IFC Productions, a venture headed by Jonathan Sehring, which will co-produce up to three features a year. Microsoft co-founder Allen, who invested $500 million in the startup DreamWorks, recently formed Clear Blue Sky Productions to develop and finance independent film projects by directors such as Sayles.

* LAS VEGAS - Chris Columbus, who last directed the comedy "Nine Months," is expected to step behind the camera for Sony TriStar Pictures' drama "Stepmom." The project will star Julia Roberts and Susan Sarandon.

* LAS VEGAS - Steve Rabineau, who has been an agent at ICM for the past 11 years, is leaving the agency and is expected to join two-year-old Endeavor as a partner. The move had been rumored for weeks.
